svg.aria-label: Japan at a glance — infographic with map, GDP bar chart and population donut chart
svg.title: Japan at a glance
svg.desc: A static editorial infographic about Japan: stylized map with major cities, country profile, GDP 2015–2024 bar chart, population donut chart and travel highlights.
svg.text: A country profile — geography, economy, people and where to go

g.text: An archipelago of four main islands
One of Japan's four largest cities
Japan is an island nation in East Asia, arcing from snowy
Hokkaido in the north to subtropical Okinawa in the south.
Roughly 124 million people crowd its Pacific coast, where
Tokyo, Yokohama, Nagoya and Osaka anchor the largest urban
A constitutional monarchy headed by an emperor, it pairs
ancient temples, castles and tea ceremonies with bullet
trains, robotics and global pop culture.
Why Japan matters — after two lost decades of deflation and a shrinking, ageing population, Japan remains the
world's fourth-largest economy and a global leader in cars, robotics, precision optics and games. Its next
chapter — demographic, digital and diplomatic — is already being written.
Japan's nominal GDP held near US$5 trillion for most of
2015–2021, peaking at US$5.12 T in 2019. Since 2022, a
weaker yen and sluggish growth have pulled the dollar
figure down to about US$4 T — behind only the US, China
A falling yen shrinks dollar GDP — output in yen terms keeps growing.
Fig. 2 — Japan's nominal GDP in current US$ trillions, 2015–2024.
Peak 2019; the 2022–24 dip mainly reflects yen depreciation. IMF WEO, Oct 2024.
Fig. 3 — Resident population by nationality, share of total, 2023 estimate.
Japan does not track ethnicity; shares are rounded estimates.
Six places for a first visit
Neon Shibuya, serene Meiji Shrine and world-class sushi.
1,600 temples, tea houses and the gates of Fushimi Inari.
Japan's street-food kitchen — takoyaki beneath the castle.
Moving peace park and the 'floating' torii of Itsukushima.
The iconic cone, onsen ryokan and Lake Ashi views.
Powder snow, flower fields and Sapporo's seafood markets.
The classic 'Golden Route' — all six fit comfortably in a two-week trip.

svg.text: Sources — GDP: IMF World Economic Outlook database (nominal GDP, current US$, Oct 2024). Population: Statistics Bureau of Japan,
Ministry of Internal Affairs & Communications (2023 estimates). Map stylized, not to scale; all figures rounded.
